page: Google Cloud Platform c3d-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the c3d server family. It features 4 vCPUs and 16 GB of RAM, translating to 4.0 GB of memory per core. The underlying hardware is powered by an AMD EPYC 9B14 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. This configuration provides 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core under a dedicated CPU allocation model. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. It lacks local storage and does not include any bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with both cached small-block and uncached large-block read/write operations scoring in the bottom 25%. For specialized tasks, the CPU supports AVX-512 vector and neural network instructions alongside cryptographic acceleration, which helps maintain average performance in Passmark encryption and physics tests.

Given its hardware profile and benchmark results, the c3d-standard-4 is suited for general-purpose workloads with moderate resource demands, such as basic web serving, text processing, and light LLM inference using small models. It is less optimal for memory-intensive databases, heavy multi-threaded compilation, or medium-to-large language model inference, where benchmarks indicate weaker performance. The instance offers a balanced resource density for entry-level enterprise applications that require dedicated CPU execution without the need for local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration.
